title: Slotless KV packing with temporal coalescing and warmup profiles to reduce fragmentation under continuous batching
creator: Maya Chen
description: Investigate and implement a 'slotless' KV cache packing strategy that reduces long-term GPU memory fragmentation caused by continuous batching and heterogeneous sequence lengths. The approach uses temporal coalescing of allocations (grouping allocations with similar lifetimes), transient padding heuristics during warmup, and a low-overhead background coalescer that runs during idle GPU cycles. This ticket covers design, prototype, benchmarks, and an opt-in rollout path.
background: We observe steadily increasing GPU memory fragmentation on hosts with mixed workloads: small-latency chat traffic interleaved with long-sequence batch jobs. Existing fixed slot / slab approaches suffer from internal fragmentation when allocation sizes don't match slot bins, and from external fragmentation when allocations live across wide lifetime ranges. Continuous batching exacerbates this: large batches allocate lots of KV shards with aligned lifetimes, while small single-shot requests create many short-lived entries. Over weeks, fragmentation increases OOM risk and forces higher headroom, increasing cost.
proposal: 1) Replace rigid slot bins for variable-sized KV entries with a slotless packed region per GPU worker. Each packed region is a monotonic arena with lightweight headers (size, epoch tag, route id). 2) Introduce temporal coalescing: when allocations are created in a short window and have similar expected lifetimes we place them adjacent to reduce holes when they free together. 3) Add transient padding during warmup: for new model/route combinations, allocate small extra slack to reduce immediate churn; the padding decays as we learn the size/lifetime distributions. 4) Background coalescer: during low-utilization epochs, perform an asynchronous compaction pass that updates indirection tables and moves cold entries to a compacted region. 5) Scheduler integration: export allocation-lifetime predictions to the request router so continuous batching groups requests with compatible lifetime profiles when latency budget allows.
design_decisions:
- Use an indirection table (per-worker) mapping logical KV keys to packed offsets. This allows moving entries without updating callers.
- Avoid global locks: use per-worker compaction tokens and epoch-based reclamation.
- Keep header metadata minimal (16 bytes) to reduce overhead.
- Coalescing threshold: default to coalescing groups of allocations that begin within 2ms and have predicted lifetime within a 10% window. Tunable via runtime config.
- Safety: compaction is non-blocking for readers; writers consult a versioned indirection and retry if migration is in-flight.
implementation_steps: Design and prototype in Rust worker: packed arena and indirection table (local branch: feature/slotless-kv)
Instrumentation: allocation-size and lifetime histogram, fragmentation ratio metric, per-route warmup profiles
Temporal coalescing policy implementation and tunable flags
Transient padding model: EMA-based decay per (model, route, sequence-length-bucket)
Background coalescer with GPU idle cycle scheduler hook
Integration with batcher: expose lifetime hints and accept batch grouping suggestions
End-to-end benchmarks (p95 latency, throughput, memory reclaimed) and canary rollout plan
Docs and runtime flags for opting into slotless mode per deployment (hosted/dedicated/private)
qa_plan:
- Unit tests for packing / indirection correctness and concurrent readers/writers.
- Fuzz tests for compaction races.
- Synthetic microbench: mixed workload generator (chat-style short requests + long-sequence bulk requests) to measure fragmentation growth over 24h.
- Performance tests asserting p95 latency regression < 5% and throughput within 3% of baseline when enabled.
- Staging canary across 2 dedicated pools for 48h with real traffic shadowing and memory telemetry comparisons.
telemetry: compaction.cycles.count: number of background coalescer runs and bytes relocated
oom_events: correlate with fragmentation and compaction activity
updates: 2026-02-21: Kickoff meeting — agreed to pursue slotless packing + temporal coalescing. Priya to own telemetry schema. (notes: doc://drive/runtime/slotless-kv-kickoff)
2026-02-28: Prototype of packed arena completed (branch pushed). Basic indirection table implemented. Observed 12% memory overhead for headers in microbench.
2026-03-03: Initial temporal coalescing policy implemented; synthetic test shows 28% slower fragmentation growth across mixed workload. Trade-off: small extra copy work on compaction.
acceptance_criteria: Fragmentation ratio reduced by >= 30% compared to baseline over 72h mixed workload
p95 token-generation latency regression <= 5% when slotless mode enabled
No increase in OOM incidents in canary clusters; memory headroom reduced by at least 10% without increase in failures
Telemetry and dashboards in place for rollout and rollback decisions
